questions.question_en: If r⃗ = x î + y ĵ + z k̂ is the position vector in R³ and r = |r⃗|, then the divergence ∇ · (r² r⃗) is equal to:
questions.question_hi:
[Mathematical Methods (Vector Identities) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
If r⃗ = x î + y ĵ + z k̂ is the position vector in R³ and r = |r⃗|, then the divergence ∇ · (r² r⃗) is equal to:
questions.explanation_en: Using ∇ · (r^n r⃗) = (n + 3) r^n: for n = 2, ∇ · (r² r⃗) = (2 + 3) r² = 5 r².
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Using ∇ · (r^n r⃗) = (n + 3) r^n: for n = 2, ∇ · (r² r⃗) = (2 + 3) r² = 5 r².

questions.question_en: The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R about an axis tangent to its surface is:
questions.question_hi:
[Mechanics (Moment of Inertia & Parallel Axis Theorem) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R about an axis tangent to its surface is:
questions.explanation_en: By the Parallel Axis Theorem, I_tangent = I_cm + M R² = (2/5) M R² + M R² = (7/5) M R².
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
By the Parallel Axis Theorem, I_tangent = I_cm + M R² = (2/5) M R² + M R² = (7/5) M R².

questions.question_en: A satellite is in a circular orbit of radius r around the Earth. The ratio of the minimum escape speed v_e from that altitude to its orbital speed v_o is:
questions.question_hi:
[Mechanics (Keplerian Orbits & Escape Velocity) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A satellite is in a circular orbit of radius r around the Earth. The ratio of the minimum escape speed v_e from that altitude to its orbital speed v_o is:
questions.explanation_en: At radius r, orbital speed is v_o = √(GM/r) and escape speed is v_e = √(2GM/r) = √2 v_o.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
At radius r, orbital speed is v_o = √(GM/r) and escape speed is v_e = √(2GM/r) = √2 v_o.

questions.question_en: Two mutually perpendicular simple harmonic oscillations x(t) = A cos(ωt) and y(t) = A cos(ωt + π/2) superpose on a particle. The resulting trajectory in the xy-plane is:
questions.question_hi:
[Oscillations & Waves (Lissajous Figures) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Two mutually perpendicular simple harmonic oscillations x(t) = A cos(ωt) and y(t) = A cos(ωt + π/2) superpose on a particle. The resulting trajectory in the xy-plane is:
options_en: a circle of radius A traversed clockwise
options_hi: a circle of radius A traversed clockwise
questions.explanation_en: Since y(t) = A cos(ωt + π/2) = −A sin(ωt), we have x² + y² = A²(cos²ωt + sin²ωt) = A², which is a circle of radius A.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since y(t) = A cos(ωt + π/2) = −A sin(ωt), we have x² + y² = A²(cos²ωt + sin²ωt) = A², which is a circle of radius A.

questions.question_en: The chromatic resolving power R = λ / Δλ of a plane transmission diffraction grating having N total ruled slits observed in the m-th order diffraction spectrum is:
questions.question_hi:
[Physical Optics (Rayleigh Criterion & Diffraction Grating) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
The chromatic resolving power R = λ / Δλ of a plane transmission diffraction grating having N total ruled slits observed in the m-th order diffraction spectrum is:
questions.explanation_en: By Rayleigh's criterion for a diffraction grating of N slits in order m, the resolving power is R = λ / Δλ = m N.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
By Rayleigh's criterion for a diffraction grating of N slits in order m, the resolving power is R = λ / Δλ = m N.

questions.question_en: A point charge +q is held at a distance d above an infinite grounded conducting plane at z = 0. The total electrostatic force of attraction experienced by the charge +q toward the conducting plane is:
questions.question_hi:
[Electricity & Magnetism (Method of Images) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A point charge +q is held at a distance d above an infinite grounded conducting plane at z = 0. The total electrostatic force of attraction experienced by the charge +q toward the conducting plane is:
questions.explanation_en: By the method of images, the grounded plane at z = 0 is replaced by an image charge −q at z = −d (separation 2d from +q). Thus F = q² / [4π ε0 (2d)²] = q² / (16π ε0 d²).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
By the method of images, the grounded plane at z = 0 is replaced by an image charge −q at z = −d (separation 2d from +q). Thus F = q² / [4π ε0 (2d)²] = q² / (16π ε0 d²).

questions.question_en: A steady current I flows around a square wire loop of side length a. The magnitude of the magnetic field B at the center of the square loop is:
questions.question_hi:
[Electromagnetism (Biot-Savart Law for Square Loop) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A steady current I flows around a square wire loop of side length a. The magnitude of the magnetic field B at the center of the square loop is:
questions.explanation_en: Each of the 4 sides is at perpendicular distance d = a/2 from the center and subtends angles θ1 = θ2 = 45° (sin 45° = 1/√2). Thus B = 4 × [μ0 I / (4π (a/2))](sin 45° + sin 45°) = (2√2 μ0 I) / (π a).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Each of the 4 sides is at perpendicular distance d = a/2 from the center and subtends angles θ1 = θ2 = 45° (sin 45° = 1/√2). Thus B = 4 × [μ0 I / (4π (a/2))](sin 45° + sin 45°) = (2√2 μ0 I) / (π a).

questions.question_en: For an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at temperature T, the correct ascending order of most probable speed (v_mp), average speed (v_avg), and root-mean-square speed (v_rms) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Kinetic Theory of Gases (Maxwell-Boltzmann Speeds) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
For an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at temperature T, the correct ascending order of most probable speed (v_mp), average speed (v_avg), and root-mean-square speed (v_rms) is:
questions.explanation_en: In the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution, v_mp : v_avg : v_rms = √2 : √(8/π) : √3 ≈ 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732, so v_mp < v_avg < v_rms.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
In the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution, v_mp : v_avg : v_rms = √2 : √(8/π) : √3 ≈ 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732, so v_mp < v_avg < v_rms.

questions.question_en: Because the molar volume of liquid water is smaller than that of solid ice at 0 °C (V_liquid < V_solid), increasing the external pressure P on an ice-water equilibrium mixture causes the melting temperature T_m of ice to:
questions.question_hi:
[Thermodynamics (Clausius-Clapeyron Equation) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Because the molar volume of liquid water is smaller than that of solid ice at 0 °C (V_liquid < V_solid), increasing the external pressure P on an ice-water equilibrium mixture causes the melting temperature T_m of ice to:
questions.explanation_en: By the Clausius-Clapeyron equation, dP/dT = L / [T (V_liquid − V_solid)]. Since L > 0 and V_liquid − V_solid < 0 for water, dT_m/dP < 0 (regelation).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
By the Clausius-Clapeyron equation, dP/dT = L / [T (V_liquid − V_solid)]. Since L > 0 and V_liquid − V_solid < 0 for water, dT_m/dP < 0 (regelation).

questions.question_en: In Compton scattering of an X-ray photon off a stationary free electron (Compton wavelength λ_C = h / (m_e c) = 0.0243 Å), the maximum possible wavelength shift Δλ_max occurs at scattering angle θ = 180° (backscattering) and equals:
questions.question_hi:
[Modern Physics (Compton Scattering) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In Compton scattering of an X-ray photon off a stationary free electron (Compton wavelength λ_C = h / (m_e c) = 0.0243 Å), the maximum possible wavelength shift Δλ_max occurs at scattering angle θ = 180° (backscattering) and equals:
questions.explanation_en: From Δλ = λ_C (1 − cos θ), the maximum occurs at θ = 180° where cos(180°) = −1, giving Δλ_max = 2 λ_C ≈ 0.0486 Å.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
From Δλ = λ_C (1 − cos θ), the maximum occurs at θ = 180° where cos(180°) = −1, giving Δλ_max = 2 λ_C ≈ 0.0486 Å.

questions.question_en: A particle of mass m is confined to a 1D infinite square well of width L. If the width of the well is doubled from L to 2L, the ground-state energy E_1 changes by a factor of:
questions.question_hi:
[Modern Physics (Quantum Tunneling & Box) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A particle of mass m is confined to a 1D infinite square well of width L. If the width of the well is doubled from L to 2L, the ground-state energy E_1 changes by a factor of:
questions.explanation_en: Since E_n = n² π² ℏ² / (2 m L²) ∝ 1 / L², doubling L reduces the ground-state energy to 1/4 of its original value.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since E_n = n² π² ℏ² / (2 m L²) ∝ 1 / L², doubling L reduces the ground-state energy to 1/4 of its original value.

questions.question_en: In an intrinsic semiconductor with energy bandgap E_g at temperature T (assuming effective masses m_e* = m_h*), the Fermi level E_F lies:
questions.question_hi:
[Solid State Physics (Intrinsic Semiconductors) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In an intrinsic semiconductor with energy bandgap E_g at temperature T (assuming effective masses m_e* = m_h*), the Fermi level E_F lies:
options_en: exactly at the midpoint of the forbidden bandgap, (E_c + E_v) / 2
just below the conduction band edge E_c
just above the valence band edge E_v
options_hi: exactly at the midpoint of the forbidden bandgap, (E_c + E_v) / 2
just below the conduction band edge E_c
just above the valence band edge E_v
questions.explanation_en: Since E_F = (E_c + E_v)/2 + (3/4) k_B T ln(m_h* / m_e*), when m_e* = m_h*, the second term vanishes and E_F lies exactly at mid-gap.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since E_F = (E_c + E_v)/2 + (3/4) k_B T ln(m_h* / m_e*), when m_e* = m_h*, the second term vanishes and E_F lies exactly at mid-gap.

questions.question_en: A 6 V Zener diode is used in a shunt voltage regulator circuit with a series resistor R_s = 200 Ω connected to an unregulated DC input V_in = 12 V, and a load resistor R_L = 600 Ω across the Zener diode. The Zener current I_Z is:
questions.question_hi:
[Electronics (Zener Diode Voltage Regulator) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A 6 V Zener diode is used in a shunt voltage regulator circuit with a series resistor R_s = 200 Ω connected to an unregulated DC input V_in = 12 V, and a load resistor R_L = 600 Ω across the Zener diode. The Zener current I_Z is:
questions.explanation_en: Since the open-circuit load voltage 12 × (600/800) = 9 V > 6 V, the Zener diode is in breakdown with V_L = V_Z = 6 V. Series current I_s = (12 − 6)/200 = 30 mA. Load current I_L = 6 / 600 = 10 mA. Thus I_Z = I_s − I_L = 30 − 10 = 20 mA.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since the open-circuit load voltage 12 × (600/800) = 9 V > 6 V, the Zener diode is in breakdown with V_L = V_Z = 6 V. Series current I_s = (12 − 6)/200 = 30 mA. Load current I_L = 6 / 600 = 10 mA. Thus I_Z = I_s − I_L = 30 − 10 = 20 mA.

questions.question_en: For laminar, incompressible viscous flow through a horizontal cylindrical pipe of radius R under a constant pressure gradient, the volumetric flow rate Q scales with the pipe radius R as:

For laminar, incompressible viscous flow through a horizontal cylindrical pipe of radius R under a constant pressure gradient, the volumetric flow rate Q scales with the pipe radius R as:

questions.question_en: Which of the following statement(s) about an isolated metallic conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is/are ALWAYS true?
questions.question_hi:
[Electromagnetism (Electrostatic Conductors) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Which of the following statement(s) about an isolated metallic conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is/are ALWAYS true?
options_en: The electric field E⃗ inside the bulk material of the conductor is identically zero.
Any net excess electric charge resides entirely on the outer surface of the conductor.
The entire conductor (surface and interior) is an equipotential volume, and E⃗ just outside the surface is normal to the surface of magnitude σ / ε0.
The surface charge density σ is always uniform over the surface regardless of the conductor's curvature.
options_hi: The electric field E⃗ inside the bulk material of the conductor is identically zero.
Any net excess electric charge resides entirely on the outer surface of the conductor.
The entire conductor (surface and interior) is an equipotential volume, and E⃗ just outside the surface is normal to the surface of magnitude σ / ε0.
The surface charge density σ is always uniform over the surface regardless of the conductor's curvature.
questions.explanation_en: Inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium E⃗ = 0⃗, the volume is equipotential, all net charge sits on the surface, and E_⊥ = σ/ε0. On non-spherical conductors, σ is highest at sharp points (high curvature), so D is false.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium E⃗ = 0⃗, the volume is equipotential, all net charge sits on the surface, and E_⊥ = σ/ε0. On non-spherical conductors, σ is highest at sharp points (high curvature), so D is false.

questions.question_en: During a reversible adiabatic (isentropic) expansion of an ideal gas with constant heat capacity ratio γ = C_P / C_V > 1, which of the following relation(s) hold(s)?
questions.question_hi:
[Thermodynamics (Reversible Adiabatic Process) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
During a reversible adiabatic (isentropic) expansion of an ideal gas with constant heat capacity ratio γ = C_P / C_V > 1, which of the following relation(s) hold(s)?
options_en: Entropy of the gas remains constant (ΔS = 0) while temperature T decreases.
Internal energy of the gas remains constant (ΔU = 0).
options_hi: Entropy of the gas remains constant (ΔS = 0) while temperature T decreases.
Internal energy of the gas remains constant (ΔU = 0).
questions.explanation_en: For a reversible adiabatic expansion (δQ_rev = 0), dS = 0, PV^γ = const, TV^(γ−1) = const, and since the gas does positive work (W > 0), ΔU = −W < 0 so T decreases.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
For a reversible adiabatic expansion (δQ_rev = 0), dS = 0, PV^γ = const, TV^(γ−1) = const, and since the gas does positive work (W > 0), ΔU = −W < 0 so T decreases.

questions.question_en: When unpolarized light travelling in air (n1 = 1) is incident on a glass surface of refractive index n2 = √3 at the Brewster (polarizing) angle θ_B, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Physical Optics (Polarization & Brewster's Law) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
When unpolarized light travelling in air (n1 = 1) is incident on a glass surface of refractive index n2 = √3 at the Brewster (polarizing) angle θ_B, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
options_en: The Brewster angle of incidence is θ_B = 60°.
The reflected ray is 100% linearly polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence (s-polarized).
The reflected ray and the refracted ray are mutually perpendicular (θ_B + θ_r = 90°).
The refracted ray is completely extinguished (zero intensity).
options_hi: The Brewster angle of incidence is θ_B = 60°.
The reflected ray is 100% linearly polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence (s-polarized).
The reflected ray and the refracted ray are mutually perpendicular (θ_B + θ_r = 90°).
The refracted ray is completely extinguished (zero intensity).
questions.explanation_en: By Brewster's Law, tan(θ_B) = n2 / n1 = √3 => θ_B = 60°. At θ_B, the reflected and refracted rays make a 90° angle (60° + 30° = 90°), and the reflected ray is purely s-polarized.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
By Brewster's Law, tan(θ_B) = n2 / n1 = √3 => θ_B = 60°. At θ_B, the reflected and refracted rays make a 90° angle (60° + 30° = 90°), and the reflected ray is purely s-polarized.

questions.question_en: In Einstein's photoelectric effect experiment (K_max = h ν − φ0 for ν > ν0), which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Modern Physics (Photoelectric Effect) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In Einstein's photoelectric effect experiment (K_max = h ν − φ0 for ν > ν0), which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
options_en: The stopping potential V_0 increases linearly with the frequency ν of incident light above threshold frequency ν0.
Increasing the intensity of incident light (at fixed frequency ν > ν0) increases the saturation photocurrent but does NOT change the stopping potential V_0.
The slope of the stopping potential V_0 versus frequency ν graph is h / e, which is universal for all target metals.
Photoemission displays a long time delay of several minutes when incident light intensity is very low.
options_hi: The stopping potential V_0 increases linearly with the frequency ν of incident light above threshold frequency ν0.
Increasing the intensity of incident light (at fixed frequency ν > ν0) increases the saturation photocurrent but does NOT change the stopping potential V_0.
The slope of the stopping potential V_0 versus frequency ν graph is h / e, which is universal for all target metals.
Photoemission displays a long time delay of several minutes when incident light intensity is very low.
questions.explanation_en: From e V_0 = h ν − φ0, V_0 increases linearly with ν with universal slope h/e, intensity controls photon flux (photocurrent) without changing K_max, and emission is instantaneous.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
From e V_0 = h ν − φ0, V_0 increases linearly with ν with universal slope h/e, intensity controls photon flux (photocurrent) without changing K_max, and emission is instantaneous.

questions.question_en: Which of the following statement(s) regarding Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) amplifier configurations is/are TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Electronics (BJT & Amplifier Configurations) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Which of the following statement(s) regarding Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) amplifier configurations is/are TRUE?
options_en: The Common-Emitter (CE) amplifier provides both voltage gain > 1 and current gain > 1, and introduces a 180° phase inversion between input and output voltages.
The Common-Collector (CC / Emitter Follower) configuration has high input impedance, low output impedance, and a non-inverting voltage gain slightly less than 1.
The current transfer ratios α = I_C / I_E and β = I_C / I_B are related by β = α / (1 − α).
In the active region of operation, both the emitter-base junction and collector-base junction are reverse biased.
options_hi: The Common-Emitter (CE) amplifier provides both voltage gain > 1 and current gain > 1, and introduces a 180° phase inversion between input and output voltages.
The Common-Collector (CC / Emitter Follower) configuration has high input impedance, low output impedance, and a non-inverting voltage gain slightly less than 1.
The current transfer ratios α = I_C / I_E and β = I_C / I_B are related by β = α / (1 − α).
In the active region of operation, both the emitter-base junction and collector-base junction are reverse biased.
questions.explanation_en: CE provides 180° phase inversion and high power gain; CC (emitter follower) acts as a buffer with unity voltage gain; β = α/(1−α). In the active region, the E-B junction is forward biased and C-B junction is reverse biased.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
CE provides 180° phase inversion and high power gain; CC (emitter follower) acts as a buffer with unity voltage gain; β = α/(1−α). In the active region, the E-B junction is forward biased and C-B junction is reverse biased.

questions.question_en: If the 2 × 2 matrix M = [[4, 2], [1, 3]] has eigenvalues λ1 and λ2 (with λ1 > λ2), then the value of (λ1 − λ2) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Mathematical Methods (Matrix Trace & Eigenvalues) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
If the 2 × 2 matrix M = [[4, 2], [1, 3]] has eigenvalues λ1 and λ2 (with λ1 > λ2), then the value of (λ1 − λ2) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Characteristic equation: λ² − 7λ + (12 − 2) = λ² − 7λ + 10 = (λ − 5)(λ − 2) = 0. Thus λ1 = 5, λ2 = 2, and λ1 − λ2 = 3.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Characteristic equation: λ² − 7λ + (12 − 2) = λ² − 7λ + 10 = (λ − 5)(λ − 2) = 0. Thus λ1 = 5, λ2 = 2, and λ1 − λ2 = 3.

questions.question_en: An alpha particle (charge q = 2e, mass m = 4 m_p) and a proton (charge e, mass m_p) are accelerated from rest through the same electrostatic potential difference V. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the proton to that of the alpha particle (λ_p / λ_α, rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Modern Physics (de Broglie Wavelength) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
An alpha particle (charge q = 2e, mass m = 4 m_p) and a proton (charge e, mass m_p) are accelerated from rest through the same electrostatic potential difference V. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the proton to that of the alpha particle (λ_p / λ_α, rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since λ = h / √(2 m q V) ∝ 1 / √(m q), we have λ_p / λ_α = √[(m_α q_α) / (m_p q_p)] = √[4 × 2] = √8 = 2√2 ≈ 2.83.

questions.question_en: For an ideal diatomic gas with 5 active degrees of freedom (3 translational + 2 rotational) at room temperature, the ratio of specific heats γ = C_P / C_V is ________.

questions.question_en: A series RLC circuit has inductance L = 10 mH, capacitance C = 1.0 μF, and resistance R = 5.0 Ω. The quality factor Q of the circuit at series resonance is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Electricity & Magnetism (RLC Resonance Quality Factor) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A series RLC circuit has inductance L = 10 mH, capacitance C = 1.0 μF, and resistance R = 5.0 Ω. The quality factor Q of the circuit at series resonance is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Resonant angular frequency ω0 = 1/√(LC) = 1/√(10⁻² × 10⁻⁶) = 10⁴ rad/s. Quality factor Q = (ω0 L)/R = (10⁴ × 0.01) / 5.0 = 100 / 5 = 20.

questions.question_en: Given that the ground-state ionization energy of a Hydrogen atom (Z = 1) is 13.6 eV, the energy (in eV) required to remove the single remaining electron from a ground-state He⁺ ion (Z = 2) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Modern Physics (Bohr Hydrogen Atom Ionization) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Given that the ground-state ionization energy of a Hydrogen atom (Z = 1) is 13.6 eV, the energy (in eV) required to remove the single remaining electron from a ground-state He⁺ ion (Z = 2) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: For a hydrogenic ion of atomic number Z, E_1(Z) = −13.6 Z² eV. For He⁺ (Z = 2), the ionization energy is 13.6 × 2² = 54.4 eV.

questions.question_en: A ball of mass m moving with speed u makes a head-on elastic collision with a stationary ball of mass 3m. The fraction of the initial kinetic energy transferred to the stationary ball of mass 3m is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Mechanics (Elastic Collision in 1D) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A ball of mass m moving with speed u makes a head-on elastic collision with a stationary ball of mass 3m. The fraction of the initial kinetic energy transferred to the stationary ball of mass 3m is ________.
questions.explanation_en: In a 1D head-on elastic collision with a stationary target, the fraction of kinetic energy transferred is 4 m1 m2 / (m1 + m2)² = 4 m (3m) / (4m)² = 12 / 16 = 0.75.

questions.question_en: An n-type semiconductor sample has a free electron concentration of n = 5.0 × 10²¹ m⁻³. Given elementary charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the magnitude of its Hall coefficient |R_H| = 1/(n e) expressed in units of 10⁻³ m³ C⁻¹ (rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Solid State Physics (Hall Coefficient) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
An n-type semiconductor sample has a free electron concentration of n = 5.0 × 10²¹ m⁻³. Given elementary charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the magnitude of its Hall coefficient |R_H| = 1/(n e) expressed in units of 10⁻³ m³ C⁻¹ (rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: |R_H| = 1 / (5.0 × 10²¹ m⁻³ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) = 1 / 800 m³ C⁻¹ = 1.25 × 10⁻³ m³ C⁻¹, so the numerical value in units of 10⁻³ m³ C⁻¹ is 1.25.

questions.question_en: In a Newton's rings experiment using monochromatic light, if the diameter of the 4th dark ring is 4.0 mm, then the diameter (in mm) of the 9th dark ring is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Physical Optics (Newton's Rings Radius) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In a Newton's rings experiment using monochromatic light, if the diameter of the 4th dark ring is 4.0 mm, then the diameter (in mm) of the 9th dark ring is ________.
questions.explanation_en: The diameter of the n-th dark ring in reflected light is proportional to √n (D_n = 2√(n R λ)). Therefore, D_9 / D_4 = √(9 / 4) = 3 / 2 => D_9 = (3/2) × 4.0 mm = 6.0 mm.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
The diameter of the n-th dark ring in reflected light is proportional to √n (D_n = 2√(n R λ)). Therefore, D_9 / D_4 = √(9 / 4) = 3 / 2 => D_9 = (3/2) × 4.0 mm = 6.0 mm.

questions.question_en: Two radioactive sources A (half-life T_A = 2 hours) and B (half-life T_B = 4 hours) initially contain equal numbers of radioactive nuclei (N_A(0) = N_B(0)). After 4 hours, the ratio of their activities (Activity of A / Activity of B) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Nuclear Physics (Radioactive Activity) • IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Two radioactive sources A (half-life T_A = 2 hours) and B (half-life T_B = 4 hours) initially contain equal numbers of radioactive nuclei (N_A(0) = N_B(0)). After 4 hours, the ratio of their activities (Activity of A / Activity of B) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Initial activity ratio R_A(0)/R_B(0) = (λ_A N_0)/(λ_B N_0) = T_B / T_A = 4 / 2 = 2. After t = 4 hours (which is 2 half-lives of A and 1 half-life of B), R_A(4) = R_A(0) × (1/2)² = R_A(0)/4, and R_B(4) = R_B(0) × (1/2)¹ = R_B(0)/2. Ratio = (2 / 4) / (1 / 2) = 1.0.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Initial activity ratio R_A(0)/R_B(0) = (λ_A N_0)/(λ_B N_0) = T_B / T_A = 4 / 2 = 2. After t = 4 hours (which is 2 half-lives of A and 1 half-life of B), R_A(4) = R_A(0) × (1/2)² = R_A(0)/4, and R_B(4) = R_B(0) × (1/2)¹ = R_B(0)/2. Ratio = (2 / 4) / (1 / 2) = 1.0.
